## Operating flow rate {#sec-par-flow}

The proven acceptable range of operating flow rate rests on the univariate study (@sec-flow). Every result at both ends of the range met the host cell protein criterion, so the range `{python} RNGS["flow"]` is proven acceptable for pool host cell protein. For viral clearance, the spiked run at `{python} qv("flow", FLOW_HI)` met both claims and supports the upper end of the range. A longer residence time at the lower end is not expected to lower binding, and this was not tested. The range rests on the assumption that the effect of flow rate does not depend on the other parameters, which a univariate study cannot test. Fragments were not measured in the flow-rate study, and no range of flow rate is claimed for them.

## Verification of the platform worst case {#sec-verification}

The host cell protein criteria of the Protein A pool and the cation exchange pool assume that anion exchange clears host cell protein at least `{python} PLAT`-fold, the lowest clearance of the platform. This report verifies that assumption by the rule of PCMP-001 §7.5 (@tbl-iac-verification). The clearance factor is the host cell protein of the load divided by the predicted pool value. The load is taken as the cation exchange pool of the process model at set-point, `{python} fx(HCP_LOAD, 1)` ng/mg. The factor is evaluated at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high, with the NOR and the set-point as characterized, on the model selected on the `{python} n_rsm` planned runs, the runs on which the criteria were fixed when INV-001 closed.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.worst_case_verification(["aex"]).show()
```

Within the NOR the lowest predicted clearance factor is `{python} fx(float(VH["predicted_nor"]))`, better than the platform value. The one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination is `{python} fx(B95)`-fold, also better. The model behind it meets the first three adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2, with R² minus predicted R² of `{python} fx(float(VH["r2_minus_pred_r2"]), 3)` and a lack of fit p-value of `{python} fp(float(VH["p_lack_of_fit"]))`, and it is not an exact fit. By the rule the bound replaced the platform value. The Protein A pool criterion widened from `{python} f"{PA_HCP0:,.0f}"` to `{python} f"{PA_HCP:,.0f}"` ng/mg and the cation exchange pool criterion from `{python} f"{CEX_HCP0:,.0f}"` to `{python} f"{CEX_HCP:,.0f}"` ng/mg. On all `{python} n_all` runs the bound would be `{python} fx(float(VALL["predicted_nor_bound95"]))`-fold. The bound rests on a model that meets all four adequacy criteria, and the model selected on the planned runs predicted every augmentation run inside its prediction interval (@sec-reeval).

The bound has three limits. First, it covers the NOR only. At the edges of the characterized range clearance was worse. Run `{python} EDGE_RUN`, at the low end of load pH and the high ends of both conductivities and of protein load, gave the highest pool host cell protein of the planned runs at an edge, and a clearance factor of `{python} fx(float(VH["observed_edge"]))`, below the platform value.

Second, the bound depends on the model selection. The plan's full quadratic model of the planned runs gives a bound of `{python} fx(float(VFULL["predicted_nor_bound95"]))`-fold, but it fails the limit on overfitting (`{python} fx(float(VFULL["r2_minus_pred_r2"]))`), and on that model the platform value would stand. The two upstream criteria would then have stayed at `{python} f"{PA_HCP0:,.0f}"` and `{python} f"{CEX_HCP0:,.0f}"` ng/mg, and at those criteria the scale-down models of Protein A and cation exchange would not be qualified for host cell protein (INV-002).

Third, the bound is calculated from the scale-down results, without the offset of the scale-down model. With the offset at its estimate the bound would be `{python} fx(B_EST)`-fold. At the unfavourable end of its 90 % interval, where manufacturing scale would carry the most host cell protein relative to the scale-down model, it would be `{python} fx(B_LO)`-fold, below the platform value. The rule of PCMP-001 §7.5 names no offset, and the bound in force is the one the rule gives.

Whether the bound depends on a single run was examined as PCP-008 §7 and PCMP-001 §7.5 require (@tbl-bound). In the model of the planned runs, runs `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in RI_P["over"]])` have a Cook's distance above `{python} COOK_K`/n (`{python} fx(RI_P["cook_limit"], 3)`), and neither exceeds the median of the F distribution (`{python} fx(RI_P["f_limit"], 2)`). Deleting each of the `{python} n_rsm` runs in turn gives bounds from `{python} fx(float(LOO_MIN["bound"]))`-fold, with run `{python} int(LOO_MIN["run"])` deleted, to `{python} fx(float(LOO_MAX["bound"]))`-fold, with run `{python} int(LOO_MAX["run"])` deleted. Every one is better than the platform value on a model that meets the first three criteria, so the widening does not depend on a single run.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_y = lambda b: "Yes" if b else "No"
_A = float(VH["assumed"])
_rows = [["Selected model, planned runs (in force)", str(n_rsm), fx(B95), _y(B95 > _A), "Yes"],
         ["Selected model, all runs", str(n_all), fx(float(VALL["predicted_nor_bound95"])),
          _y(float(VALL["predicted_nor_bound95"]) > _A), _y(bool(VALL["model_adequate"]))],
         [f"Run {int(LOO_MIN['run'])} deleted, lowest of the deletions", str(n_rsm - 1), fx(float(LOO_MIN["bound"])),
          _y(float(LOO_MIN["bound"]) > _A), "Yes"],
         [f"Run {int(LOO_MAX['run'])} deleted, highest of the deletions", str(n_rsm - 1), fx(float(LOO_MAX["bound"])),
          _y(float(LOO_MAX["bound"]) > _A), "Yes"]]
for run_, b_ in LOO_FLAG.items():
    _rows.append([f"Flagged run {run_} deleted", str(n_rsm - 1), fx(b_), _y(b_ > _A), "Yes"])
_rows += [["Offset applied at its estimate", str(n_rsm), fx(B_EST), _y(B_EST > _A), "Yes"],
          ["Offset applied at the unfavourable end of its 90 % interval", str(n_rsm), fx(B_LO), _y(B_LO > _A), "Yes"],
          ["Plan's full quadratic model, no selection", str(n_rsm), fx(float(VFULL["predicted_nor_bound95"])),
           _y(float(VFULL["predicted_nor_bound95"]) > _A), "No"]]
_df_bound = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Analysis", "Runs", "Bound,\nfold", "Better than\n" + PLAT + "-fold",
                                         "Model meets\ncriteria 1 to 3"])
_nt_bound = [("", "Criteria 1 to 3 of PCMP-001 §7.2, the model F-test, the lack of fit test and the limit on "
                  "overfitting. The bound in force is the first row. A deletion repeats the selection on the "
                  "remaining planned runs.")]
_al_bound = ["P{6.6cm}", "c", "r", "c", "c"]
_cap_bound = "The one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single batch for the host cell protein clearance of anion exchange, and its alternatives."
T.frame(_df_bound, _cap_bound, "tbl-bound", align=_al_bound, size="footnotesize", notes=_nt_bound, notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The widening is argued by its risk, in the four parts PCMP-001 §7.5 sets:

1. Who bears the risk. A widened criterion lets an upstream pool with slightly more host cell protein pass to the next step. A cation exchange pool at its widened criterion of `{python} f"{CEX_HCP:,.0f}"` ng/mg, cleared only at the platform worst case of `{python} PLAT`-fold, would give an anion exchange pool of `{python} fx(CEX_AT_PLATFORM, 1)` ng/mg, above the drug substance criterion. Such a batch would fail release, so the risk is the producer's.
2. Detection. Host cell protein in the drug substance is tested at release by the ELISA AMV-3012, whose LOQ of `{python} f"{HCP_LOQ:g}"` ng/mg lies far below the criterion of `{python} HCP_CRIT`. The ELISA detects `{python} f"{HCP_COV:g}"` % of the host cell protein species of the platform antigen by `{python} HCP_COV_METHOD`, and a release result describes that share of the population.
3. What the downstream steps must clear. Anion exchange is the last step that clears host cell protein, and no later step changes it on the platform. Under the widened criteria this step must clear at least `{python} fx(B95)`-fold where the platform value asked for `{python} PLAT`-fold, which is the clearance the bound shows for a single batch within the NOR.
4. The probability that the drug substance is out of specification. In the integrated process model no simulated batch exceeded `{python} HCP_CRIT`, and the tail probability of the normal distribution fitted to the batches is zero to the precision of the calculation. With no batch outside, the one-sided 95 % upper bound from the simulation is `{python} fx(UB_PCT, 2)` %. It covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated process model.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

Capability at commercial scale comes from the integrated process model of `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` simulated batches, against the drug substance criteria (@tbl-cap). Each Cpk is set against the target of `{python} f"{CPK_TARGET:g}"` and the minimum of `{python} f"{CPK_MIN:g}"` of PCMP-001 §7.9, and every attribute this step sets or clears meets the target. The cumulative MVM clearance has the lowest Cpk, `{python} CAP_TXT["lrv_mvm"]`, and the cumulative XMuLV clearance `{python} CAP_TXT["lrv_xmulv"]`. Both are cumulative over several steps, and this step contributes one claim to each. No simulated batch fell outside any criterion of the table. The normal tail probability is `{python} fx(float(POOS.loc["lrv_mvm", "ppm_normal"]), 2)` per million for MVM and `{python} fx(float(POOS.loc["lrv_xmulv", "ppm_normal"]), 2)` per million for XMuLV, and zero to the precision of the calculation for the other attributes.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for k in CAP_KEYS:
    c = CAP.loc[k]
    cpk = float(c["Cpk"])
    verdict = ("Meets the target" if cpk >= CPK_TARGET else "Below the target, above the minimum" if cpk >= CPK_MIN
               else "Below the minimum")
    acc = (f"≥ {c['acc_low']:g}" if c["spec_type"] == "lower" else f"≤ {c['acc_high']:g}") + f" {c['unit']}"
    _rows.append([c["cqa"], c["criticality"], acc, msd(k), fx(cpk, 2),
                  verdict, f"{int(POOS.loc[k, 'n_oos'])} of {int(POOS.loc[k, 'n'])}"])
_df_cap = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Criticality", "Drug substance\ncriterion", "Mean ± SD",
                                       "Cpk", f"Against {CPK_TARGET:g}\nand {CPK_MIN:g}", "Batches\noutside"])
_nt_cap = [("", f"Integrated process model of {N_MC:,} simulated batches, every parameter drawn within its NOR. "
                "Batches outside, the simulated batches outside the criterion. "
                "Viral clearance is cumulative over the steps that clear the virus. Residual DNA per dose of "
                f"{DOSE_TXT}. SD, standard deviation.")]
_al_cap = ["P{3.0cm}", "c", "P{2.2cm}", "P{2.4cm}", "r", "P{2.0cm}", "r"]
T.frame(_df_cap, "Capability at commercial scale of the attributes the anion exchange step sets or clears.", "tbl-cap", align=_al_cap, size="footnotesize", notes=_nt_cap, notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Two of the Cpk values describe assumptions more than this step. Residual DNA has a Cpk of `{python} CAP_TXT["residual_dna"]`, but the integrated process model takes the anion exchange DNA log reduction as `{python} f"{DNA_LRV_MODEL:g}"` log10, and this study can show only more than `{python} fx(DNA_LOG[1], 2)` log10 (@sec-dna). The capability of residual DNA therefore rests on that model input, which this study does not confirm. Residual DNA has no intermediate acceptance criterion, because the platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for the steps after Protein A (PCMP-001 §7.3). Leached Protein A has a Cpk of `{python} f"{CPK['leached_protein_a']:,.0f}"`, which is not meaningful for an attribute so far below its criterion. It is judged instead on the pools of this step, all below the LOQ of `{python} f"{LPA_LOQ:g}"` ppm, which lies `{python} f"{LPA_DS / LPA_LOQ:g}"` times below the drug substance criterion of `{python} f"{LPA_DS:g}"` ppm.

Pool host cell protein has a Cpk of `{python} CAP_TXT["hcp"]` in the drug substance and fragments `{python} CAP_TXT["fragments_lmw"]`. The simulation varies each parameter within its NOR and carries no source of commercial variability that the scale-down model does not reproduce. Confirmation at commercial scale is a Stage 2 activity [@fda2011].

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

Parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of the A-Mab case study as PCMP-001 §7.7 states it [@amab2009]. A parameter with a significant effect on a critical quality attribute within the characterized range is a critical process parameter. It is well controlled (WC-CPP) when its risk of falling outside its acceptable range is low, and a CPP when that risk is high. An attribute is affected by a parameter when a term that contains the parameter is significant at `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` (PCMP-001 §6.2), and this report applies that test to the selected response-surface model, the predictive model. No numerical threshold exists for how far inside its acceptable range a parameter must be held, so the margin between each NOR and its proven acceptable range is stated. All five parameters were classified as WC-CPP. A WC-CPP is a critical process parameter, so the step has five critical process parameters, all well controlled.

- Load pH (WC-CPP). Load pH acts on pool host cell protein and on both LRFs, with p < 0.001 in each selected model. Across its characterized range it multiplies pool host cell protein by `{python} fx(fold_A)` and raises the XMuLV and MVM LRFs by `{python} fx(2 * xA)` and `{python} fx(2 * mA)` log10. Its NOR lies inside every proven acceptable range. The NOR-propagated ranges for the two viruses end `{python} fx(min(MARG.values()))` pH units below the NOR, and the other ranges span the characterized range. The load is adjusted to its target pH before it is applied (PCP-008 §5.2). Load pH was classified as a WC-CPP.
- Equil/Wash-1 conductivity (WC-CPP). Equil/Wash-1 conductivity acts on pool host cell protein (p < 0.001), which it multiplies by `{python} fx(fold_B)` across its characterized range. No effect on either LRF, on step yield or on fragments was detected. Every proven acceptable range spans the characterized range, which reaches `{python} fx(MARG_PH["wash1_cond"][0], 1)` `{python} P["wash1_cond"].unit` beyond the NOR on each side. The conductivity is set when the buffer is prepared. Equil/Wash-1 conductivity was classified as a WC-CPP.
- Load conductivity (WC-CPP). Load conductivity lowers both LRFs (p < 0.001), by `{python} fx(-2 * xC)` log10 for XMuLV and `{python} fx(-2 * mC)` log10 for MVM across its characterized range. No effect on pool host cell protein, step yield or fragments was detected. Every proven acceptable range spans the characterized range, which reaches `{python} f"{MARG_PH['load_cond'][0]:g}"` `{python} P["load_cond"].unit` beyond the NOR on each side. The load is adjusted to its target conductivity before it is applied. Load conductivity was classified as a WC-CPP.
- Protein load (WC-CPP). Protein load enters the selected XMuLV model through its interaction with load pH (`{python} pe(float(XMm.pvalues["load_ph:load"]))`), which changes the LRF across the protein load range by `{python} fx(xD_lo)` to +`{python} fx(xD_hi)` log10, depending on load pH. That change is of the size of the repeatability of the XMuLV assay, and the near-equivalent XMuLV model without the interaction would leave protein load with no effect on any attribute (@sec-near). No effect on pool host cell protein, MVM, step yield or fragments was detected, and every proven acceptable range spans the characterized range. Protein load was classified as a WC-CPP on the selected model, which decides.
- Operating flow rate (WC-CPP). No effect of flow rate on pool host cell protein or step yield was detected at the two ends of its range, and the spiked run at the shortest residence time met both viral claims (@sec-flow). By the classification rule alone, this evidence would place flow rate among the general process parameters, since no effect on a critical quality attribute was demonstrated. Operating flow rate was classified as a WC-CPP. The viral clearance claims of this step were demonstrated only inside the flow-rate range studied, with a single spiked run at its upper end, and the study cannot resolve an interaction of flow rate with load pH or load conductivity, which act on clearance. Residence time is the route by which flow rate could act on viral clearance (PCP-008 §6.4).

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

This step contributes the following to the control strategy of the drug substance, which PCMR-001 consolidates.

1. Parameter ranges. Load pH, Equil/Wash-1 conductivity, load conductivity, protein load and operating flow rate are controlled within their NORs (@tbl-params), which lie inside their proven acceptable ranges and, for the four multivariate parameters, inside the design space.
2. Viral clearance. The step contributes `{python} CL_X` log10 for XMuLV and `{python} CL_M` log10 for MVM to the cumulative claims, which PCMR-001 consolidates with the claims of low-pH viral inactivation (PCR-006) and virus filtration (PCR-009). These claims hold on the mean at the worst case within the NOR and rest on the scale-down spiking model.
3. Host cell protein. The step brings host cell protein to its drug substance level. The upstream criteria of the Protein A pool (PCR-005) and the cation exchange pool (PCR-007) rely on its verified clearance of at least `{python} fx(B95)`-fold, and host cell protein is tested at drug substance release.
4. Load material. A load deamidated during an extended hold after neutralization changed the host cell protein response of the step (DEV-008-01), and the charge variant profile by icIEF (AMV-3013) detected it. This report carries forward to PCMR-001 a limit on the hold of the neutralized cation exchange pool before anion exchange.
5. Pool collection. The trailing-edge UV set-point that ends pool collection is part of SOP-2011 at its corrected value (DEV-008-02).
6. Residual DNA and leached Protein A. Both are judged at the drug substance against their criteria. The DNA capability of the drug substance rests on the DNA clearance the integrated process model assumes for this step, which this study cannot confirm (@sec-dna).
7. Resin life cycle. Resin packing, sanitization and life cycle are controlled under SOP-2008 and are outside this study.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The step behaves as a charge-based flow-through polish. Pool host cell protein depends on load pH and Equil/Wash-1 conductivity as fold changes, and both LRFs depend on load pH and load conductivity. Within the NOR every output meets its criterion. The viral clearance claims have the smallest margins, `{python} fx(WC_MEAN[XM] - CLAIM[XM])` log10 for XMuLV and `{python} fx(WC_MEAN[MV] - CLAIM[MV])` log10 for MVM at the least favourable combination, both on the side of low load pH and high load conductivity. The design space ends where those two settings meet, outside the NOR.

Confidence in the scale-down model is greatest for pool host cell protein, for which the model is qualified at its criterion with the offset at both ends of its interval. Fragments and viral clearance were not compared at the two scales. Fragments lie far below their criterion, but the expectation that the step leaves the fragment level of its load unchanged was not tested, because the load was not measured. The viral clearance results are those of a small-scale spiking study [@ichq5a], and the record holds neither the qualification of the spiking model nor the assay controls that PCP-008 required. The pressure across the bed was not measured in the qualification, and the scale-down column gave fewer plates per metre than the manufacturing columns. The pool-collection set-point of DEV-008-02 was the same in every run, so it cannot have created or hidden an effect, but its effect on the level of the outputs is not in the record.

The verification of the host cell protein clearance widened the criteria of two upstream steps. The widening does not depend on a single run, and the model behind it is adequate on all four criteria. It does depend on the model selection, and it is sensitive to the scale-down offset, at the unfavourable end of whose interval the bound would fall below the platform value. The risk of the widening is the producer's, because host cell protein is tested at drug substance release.

The first execution of the designs ran on a deamidated load and was invalidated and re-executed (DEV-008-01). Its data confirm the cause and serve no other purpose. The augmentation of `{python} PD_AUG` was decided before any new run but made after the planned results were known. For pool host cell protein and fragments the planned runs alone give the same models and the same judgements, and the augmentation changed only the model of step yield, which has no criterion. The flow-rate study ran without its centre run (`{python} PD_FLOW`), so it cannot show curvature in the effect of flow rate. The screening run of DEV-008-03 is not identified in the record. The screening results it could affect are those of MVM, step yield and fragments, and the predictive model of every output comes from the response-surface design, which the event did not affect (@sec-dev03).

Four limitations remain. The design space is not confirmed at scale at its edges, and Stage 2 confirms performance inside the NOR only. The univariate assessment of flow rate cannot detect an interaction with the other parameters. The residual DNA clearance of the step cannot be shown by an assay whose LOQ lies far above the drug substance criterion per dose, so the capability of residual DNA rests on the process model. The studies assumed that the resin performs within its qualified life cycle (PCP-008 §12), and clearance on resin near the end of its life cycle is outside them and is governed by SOP-2008.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. Load pH and Equil/Wash-1 conductivity act on pool host cell protein, multiplying it by `{python} fx(fold_A)` and `{python} fx(fold_B)` across their ranges. Load pH and load conductivity act on both LRFs. No effect on step yield or fragments was detected within the ranges studied (objective 1).
2. The design space covers `{python} fx(100 * DSF, 1)` % of the characterized region and contains the whole NOR. MVM clearance bounds it at low load pH and high load conductivity (objective 2).
3. Every proven acceptable range contains its NOR. The range of load pH carried into the control strategy is `{python} INTERSECT_PH`, and every other multivariate parameter carries its characterized range. Operating flow rate is supported across its characterized range for pool host cell protein and at its upper end for viral clearance (objective 3).
4. All five parameters were classified as WC-CPP (objective 4).
5. The step meets its claims of `{python} CL_X` log10 for XMuLV and `{python} CL_M` log10 for MVM on the mean at the worst case within the NOR, and the NORs are justified as the Stage 2 ranges (objective 5).
6. The host cell protein clearance of the step has a one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single batch of `{python} fx(B95)`-fold within the NOR, better than the platform worst case of `{python} PLAT`-fold. It widened the Protein A and cation exchange criteria. It does not depend on a single run, but it depends on the model selection and on the scale-down offset (objective 6).
7. Every attribute the step sets or clears meets the capability target of `{python} f"{CPK_TARGET:g}"`, the tightest being the cumulative MVM clearance at `{python} CAP_TXT["lrv_mvm"]`.
8. The three study events are resolved, and the three discrepancies from the plan are recorded with what they changed. The results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Study events and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-record}

A process characterization study is not GMP manufacture and raises no deviation. This report records what departed from the expected course in two registers. The study events are the events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded, under the DEV numbers it gave them. The discrepancies from the plan are every departure from PCP-008 Version 2.0, both work the plan did not foresee and a requirement of the plan that was not met. PCP-008 §7 and §9 call a departure from the plan a deviation, and this report records each such departure as a discrepancy from the plan instead.

## Study events {#sec-events}

### DEV-008-01, a non-representative load in the first execution {#sec-dev01}

The first execution of the screening and response-surface designs (study S-AEX-SUP, `{python} win("S-AEX-SUP")`) ran on a load that did not represent the process. The load lot LOT-CEX-8842 carried `{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_deamidated_pct:g}"` % acidic variants, against `{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_requalified_pct:g}"` % for the requalified lot. In that execution pool host cell protein rose steeply with protein load at high Equil/Wash-1 conductivity. The screening effect of the interaction of protein load and Equil/Wash-1 conductivity was `{python} fx(BD_SUP, 1)` ng/mg (`{python} pe(BD_SUP_P)`). Of the runs at high protein load and high Equil/Wash-1 conductivity, `{python} n_sup_over` exceeded the drug substance criterion, the highest at `{python} T.num(SUP_MAX)` ng/mg.

The event was detected during the charge-variant verification of the load material by icIEF (AMV-3013). The investigation found that the cation exchange eluate had been held for `{python} dev_008_01_neutralized_hold_h` h after neutralization, an extended hold that promoted asparagine deamidation. Under PCP-008 §7, a design executed on material outside the release profile of the cation exchange pool is invalidated for the definition of the operating region and re-executed in full on a qualified load. Both designs were therefore invalidated and re-executed on the requalified lot LOT-CEX-8851, as studies S-AEX-SCR and S-AEX-RSM. The data of the first execution are retained and were used only to confirm the cause, and no range, class or clearance claim rests on them (@tbl-doe-aex-screening-sup and @tbl-doe-aex-rsm-sup).

The requalified data confirm the cause. In the re-executed screening design the same interaction is `{python} fx(BD_REQ, 2)` ng/mg (`{python} pe(BD_REQ_P)`). In the response-surface data it is not significant on either scale, with `{python} pe(BD_R_P_LOG)` on the log scale and `{python} fp(BD_R_P_RAW)` on the raw scale in the full quadratic model, and no near-equivalent model contains it (@sec-near). No run of the re-executed designs or of the augmentation exceeded `{python} HCP_CRIT`. The interaction appeared only on the deamidated load. The first execution measured fragments by SEC, because it ran before AMD-001.

PCP-008 §7 sets no numerical limit for the release profile of the load. The record classes the first lot, at `{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_deamidated_pct:g}"` % acidic variants, as not representative and the requalified lot, at `{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_requalified_pct:g}"` %, as representative. It holds no result for the host cell protein content, protein concentration, pH or conductivity of either lot, which the same item of PCP-008 lists.

### DEV-008-02, the pool-collection set-point {#sec-dev02}

In both executions of the designs, the trailing-edge UV set-point that ends pool collection was `{python} dev_008_02_uv_pool_stop_original_mau` mAU, against the corrected set-point of `{python} dev_008_02_uv_pool_stop_corrected_mau` mAU. The event was detected during the reconciliation of the pool fractions after execution, with host cell protein measured by ELISA (AMV-3012). The cause was a set-point in the method that was slightly permissive. The record gives the outcome as corrected by modelling and verification runs, and it names `{python} dev_008_02_ver_n` verification runs. It does not hold their results, and this report does not use them.

The set-point was the same in every run of both executions. It therefore acts on all runs alike and does not enter the estimated effects or the terms of the selected models, which come from differences between runs. It can shift the level of an output, and the record gives no size for that shift at the corrected set-point. For pool host cell protein the upper 95 % limit of a single run over the NOR leaves a factor of `{python} fx(MARGIN_HCP, 1)` to the criterion. The viral clearance claims have the smallest margins, and the effect of the set-point on the LRFs is not in the record. The runs of the re-executed designs are analysed as recorded.

### DEV-008-03, an equilibration and wash buffer below its pH range {#sec-dev03}

The equilibration and first wash buffer used on one screening run, lot LOT-BUF-8815, had a pH of `{python} f"{dev_008_03_buffer_ph_measured:g}"` at release testing under SOP-2103 (`{python} PRIOR.loc["SOP-2103", "title"]`), below its acceptance limit of `{python} f"{dev_008_03_buffer_ph_low_limit:g}"` and its target of `{python} f"{dev_008_03_buffer_ph_target:g}"`. The cause was an error at the titration end point during buffer preparation. The run was retained in the analysis.

The buffer pH is not a factor of the designs, so no setting correction applies. A lower buffer pH weakens the binding of acidic impurities during equilibration and the chase, in the same direction as a lower load pH. The record does not name the run, so it cannot be marked in Appendix A, analysed with its result excluded or compared with its model prediction. Each of the `{python} n_scr` screening runs was therefore deleted in turn. The significant terms of pool host cell protein and XMuLV did not change with any deletion, so those screening results do not depend on the affected run, whichever it was. For MVM, step yield and fragments the set of significant terms changed with `{python} SCR_LOO_N[MV]`, `{python} SCR_LOO_N[YLD]` and `{python} SCR_LOO_N[FRAG]` of the deletions. The event affected the screening design only, which identifies effects and sets no range. Every prediction, range and judgement of this report comes from the response-surface design, which the event did not affect.

## Discrepancies from the plan {#sec-discrepancies}

@tbl-discrepancies lists the `{python} n_pd` discrepancies from PCP-008.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(discrepancy_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Discrepancies of the anion exchange characterization from its plan PCP-008. {#tbl-discrepancies}")
```

The augmentation, `{python} PD_AUG` (@sec-rsm-design), was work the plan did not foresee. INV-002 decided its rule on `{python} MA["decided"]`, before any new run, and the runs were made from `{python} W[AUG_ID][0]` to `{python} W[AUG_ID][1]`, after the planned results were known. What it changed was computed (@sec-reeval). For pool host cell protein the selected model has the same scale and terms on the planned runs alone, and on them the criterion is met over the NOR and the scale-down model is qualified. For fragments the selected model has no term on either set of runs. Step yield has no adequate model on the planned runs alone and an adequate model with no term on all runs.

The model selection, `{python} PD_SEL` (@sec-stats), replaced the plan's full quadratic model for every output. On the planned runs the full quadratic models of all four outputs with a criterion fail the limit on overfitting. PCMP-001 §7.2 allows such a model to be refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation, and the selection is the procedure INV-002 corrective action CA3 applies for it. At this step no criterion moved, and no judgement over the NOR differs between the criteria in force and the criteria as they would be without the selection. The selection does decide whether the host cell protein bound of this step widens the upstream criteria, and with them whether the scale-down models of Protein A and cation exchange are qualified for host cell protein (@sec-verification).

The flow-rate study, `{python} PD_FLOW` (@sec-uni-design), ran each end of its range in duplicate and made no run at its centre. The qualification runs at set-point (S-AEX-SDM, `{python} win("S-AEX-SDM")`) serve as the reference, and they were made before the designs began. The comparison between the two ends does not need a centre run, and neither difference was significant (@sec-flow). Without a centre run the study cannot show curvature in the effect of flow rate within the range.

# Appendix C — Full effect and coefficient tables {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for r in RESP + [FRAG]:
    k = 100.0 if r == YLD else 1.0
    for _, x in SEFF[r].iterrows():
        _rows.append([f"{RL[r]} ({RU[r]})", x["Term"], fx(x["Effect"] * k, 3), fx(x["Coef."] * k, 3),
                      fx(x["Std. err."] * k, 3), fx(x["t"], 2), fp(x["p-value"])])
_df_eff = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Output", "Term", "Effect", "Coefficient", "Std. err.", "t", "p"])
_nt_eff = [("", "Coded units. A, load pH. B, Equil/Wash-1 conductivity. C, load conductivity. D, protein load. "
                "Two letters, the interaction of the two parameters. An effect is twice the coefficient.")]

T.frame(_df_eff, "Screening effects of every anion exchange output.", "tbl-effects-all", merge=["Output"], align=_al_eff, size="footnotesize", notes=_nt_eff, notes_per_row=True).show()
```

# Appendix D — Analytical methods summary {.unnumbered}

@tbl-methods-summary summarises the methods behind the responses of this report, with the precision and LOQ of each from its validation record.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_amv = dict(AEX_AMV_REFS)
_use = [("AMV-3012", "Pool host cell protein", "ng/mg"), ("AMV-3014", "Residual DNA, load and pool", "pg/mg"),
        ("AMV-3016", "Leached Protein A, load and pool", "ppm"), ("AMV-3017", "XMuLV infectivity, spiked load and pool", "log10"),
        ("AMV-3018", "MVM infectivity, spiked load and pool", "log10"), ("AMV-3013", "Charge variants of the load", "%"),
        ("AMV-3020", "Fragments (LMW) in the pool", "%")]
_rows = []
for aid, what, unit in _use:
    if aid == "AMV-3020":
        prec, loq = f"SD {CESDS['sd_abs']:g} {unit}", f"{CESDS['loq']:g} {unit}"
    else:
        m = METH.loc[aid]
        prec = (f"{float(m['precision_pct']):g} log10" if unit == "log10" else f"{float(m['precision_pct']):g} % CV")
        loq = f"{float(m['loq']):g} {m['loq_unit']}"
    _rows.append([aid, _amv[aid], what, prec, loq])
_df_meth = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Method", "Title", "Measured in this report", "Precision", "LOQ"])
_nt_meth = [("", "Precision from the validation record of each method, as a coefficient of variation, CV, as a "
                 "repeatability in log10 for the infectivity assays, or as a standard deviation, SD, for "
                 "nrCE-SDS. The performance characteristics are held in the validation reports.")]
_al_meth = ["l", "P{3.6cm}", "P{3.6cm}", "P{2.0cm}", "P{2.6cm}"]
T.frame(_df_meth, "Analytical methods behind the responses of the anion exchange characterization.", "tbl-methods-summary", align=_al_meth, size="footnotesize", notes=_nt_meth, notes_per_row=True).show()
```
